title: Breeding NONcNZO10/LtJ and NON/ShiLtJ Mice
author: Ian Simpson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.556g89e

steps.title: Set up breeding pairs
steps.instruction: Breed mice at 6–7 weeks of age or older by placing two females with one male. Purchase new male and female breeders from JAX Laboratories every 6 months.

steps.title: Maintain breeding pairs for five days
steps.instruction: Set up the breeding cages on a Thursday; keep the male with the females for five days, then separate the male on the following Tuesday while the females remain together.

steps.title: Prepare cages before expected birth
steps.instruction: The Friday before the females are due to have pups, change the cages, provide fresh water, fill the food hopper, check which females are pregnant, and place a “Do Not Disturb” sign on each cage.

steps.title: Monitor litters during birth week
steps.instruction: During the week the females start having pups, avoid moving cages in and out; simply look into the cages to detect litters.

steps.title: Post‑birth care week
steps.instruction: One week after the pups are born, remove the “Do Not Disturb” sign and refill water bottles and food hoppers as needed.

steps.title: Separate double‑litters at 2–2.5 weeks
steps.instruction: If a cage contains two litters, sex the pups at 2 to 2.5 weeks of age, then divide male pups evenly between the two cages (keep any extra male as a breeder). Next, distribute females evenly so each dam has the same number of pups.

steps.title: Wean pups at four weeks
steps.instruction: Wean the mice at 4 weeks of age (±1 day). Pair male pups; any odd male is retained as a breeder. House females together, up to five per cage.

steps.title: Switch experimental mice to autoclaved diet
steps.instruction: At weaning, place experimental NON/NZ and NON/Shi mice on autoclaved 5K20 diet (Animals Specialties and Provisions, LLC) for 20 min at 120 °C. Keep all breeder mice on 2016 diet (Harlan Laboratories).

steps.title: Ear‑tag and weigh experimental mice
steps.instruction: Ear‑tag mice in pairs: assign the lowest tag number to the left ear of the first mouse and the highest number to the right ear of the second mouse. For each pair, ear‑tag the first mouse, weigh it, and place it in a new cage; then ear‑tag the second mouse, weigh it, and place it in the same cage. Repeat with subsequent pairs.

substeps.instruction: Ear‑tag first mouse (lowest tag number) in left ear.
Weigh first mouse and place in new cage.
Ear‑tag second mouse (highest tag number) in right ear.
Weigh second mouse and place with first mouse.

steps.title: Place weaned females and male breeders on 2916 diet
steps.instruction: Wean female mice at this time and put them on 2916 diet; they do not require weighing or blood‑glucose measurement. Also place male breeders on 2916 diet with the same exemptions.

steps.title: Bi‑weekly weighing during early diet phase
steps.instruction: Weigh all mice every other week for the first four weeks while they are on the 5K20 diet.

steps.title: Add nestlet at six weeks
steps.instruction: At six weeks on the 5K20 diet, place a nestlet into each experimental mouse cage and remove the nesting sheets.

steps.title: Weigh and measure glucose from eight to fourteen weeks
steps.instruction: At eight weeks of age, and then every other week thereafter until fourteen weeks, weigh the mice and check blood‑glucose levels while they remain on the 5K20 diet.

steps.title: Perform measurements before ten am
steps.instruction: Conduct all weighings and blood‑glucose measurements before 10:00 am.

steps.title: Transfer mice for experimentation
steps.instruction: Move mice on Thursdays, usually at nineteen weeks of age, to the CG740H facility in the CAQ for experimentation.

steps.title: Classify diabetic versus control mice
steps.instruction: Mice with blood‑glucose levels ≥250 mg/dL are classified as diabetic; those with levels <250 mg/dL are controls.
